candidates.basis: The NL6 termination contract names HighwayMode and FinishState as a termination relation. The closed inspection inventory binds FinishState to state:FinishState:line:21 and records outgoing transition:line:36 and transition:line:40. The source inventory also identifies FinishState as the HighwayMode completion target.
candidates.expected: HighwayMode must terminate by reaching a stable FinishState with no continuation that re-enters or exits into continued behavior.
candidates.observed: FinishState is reachable but has outgoing transitions to the enclosing final boundary on `urban_way=true` and `auto_finished=true`; the target is therefore not stable termination in the supplied closed model.
candidates.reason: The required termination property is stronger than endpoint existence. The exact closed model reaches FinishState, but FinishState has outgoing transitions to the enclosing completion boundary under `urban_way=true` and `auto_finished=true`, so the designated completion state can continue rather than remain a stable termination point.
candidates.requirement_quote: The HighwayMode ends when the system transitions to FinishState, triggered by the `auto_finished=true` condition.
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The authored source explicitly describes HighwayMode as ending at FinishState, and the endpoint transition exists; if termination is interpreted as eventual entry only rather than stable completion, the outgoing FinishState behavior would not refute it.
candidates.title: HighwayMode does not stably terminate at FinishState

candidates.basis: NL12 defines the collision avoidance system scope and its two states. The source inventory and trace bind CollisionAvoidance plus both child states to exact closed refs. Inspection-equivalent and finite verification facts report CollisionAvoidance and both children unreachable from a top-level initial entry.
candidates.expected: The collision avoidance states must be operationally available within the collision avoidance system scope.
candidates.observed: CollisionAvoidance, collision_avoidance_deactive, and collision_avoidance_active are structurally present and nested, but all three are unreachable from the top-level initial entry.
candidates.reason: The exact collision avoidance scope and both required states are present and contained, but the enclosing CollisionAvoidance composite is absent from top-level reachability. This is a behavioral scope consequence distinct from declaration or containment.
candidates.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance states must be contained within the collision avoidance system scope.
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The contract property itself is containment, and the supplied model does satisfy structural containment; the reachability fact may be a separate behavioral concern rather than a failure of containment.
candidates.title: Collision avoidance scope is unreachable from the root

candidates.basis: NL12 requires initial entry into collision_avoidance_deactive within the collision avoidance system. The closed model binds the local edge to transition:line:86 and its owner to CollisionAvoidance, while inspection-equivalent and verification facts show the owner and target are unreachable from top-level initialization.
candidates.expected: The collision avoidance system must be entered from the top-level initialization context and then enter collision_avoidance_deactive.
candidates.observed: The local initial edge exists, but CollisionAvoidance and collision_avoidance_deactive are unreachable from the top-level initial entry; no operational root path reaches this owner-local entry.
candidates.reason: The authored collision avoidance scope has an exact local initial edge to collision_avoidance_deactive, but that scope itself is not reached from the top-level initial entry. A local child entry therefore does not establish operational root entry for the collision avoidance system.
candidates.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system must initially enter collision_avoidance_deactive.
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The exact owner-local initial edge is present and unconditional, so the narrow local initial-entry relation is satisfied if root reachability is outside the contract's intended scope.
candidates.title: Collision avoidance has no reachable root entry

candidates.observed: The declared activation consumer transition:line:87 exists, but its consumer state and transition are not reachable from a top-level initial entry.

issues.basis: NL6, exact_source_inventory transition tr_0009/tr_0012/tr_0029, FCSTM transitions transition:line:75 and transition:line:76, and exact HighwayMode/FinishState bindings.
issues.expected: A transition whose source is HighwayMode and whose target is FinishState must exist for the `auto_finished=true` completion behavior.
issues.observed: The closed model's HighwayMode completion carrier at transition:line:75 resolves from HighwayMode to `[*]`; the model's FinishState entry transitions are pseudostate-to-FinishState and are not HighwayMode-to-FinishState.
issues.reason: The author-source requirement names FinishState as the completion target. The closed model has an exact HighwayMode-to-completion transition carrier, but its resolved target is the final pseudostate rather than FinishState; the source requirement is therefore not closed by that carrier.
issues.requirement_quote: The HighwayMode ends when the system transitions to FinishState, triggered by the `auto_finished=true` condition.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The generated route-control sequence may be intended to route through FinishState indirectly, but the supplied closed transition inventory does not establish that indirect path as the required direct HighwayMode-to-FinishState endpoint.
issues.title: HighwayMode completion uses an exit instead of FinishState

issues.basis: NL12 names the collision avoidance system and its two states; exact_source_inventory and source_trace establish the scope; inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts refute root reachability for CollisionAvoidance and both descendants.
issues.expected: The CollisionAvoidance scope must be reachable from a top-level initial entry so its required behavior can execute.
issues.observed: state:CollisionAvoidance:line:83 is marked `reachable_from_initial=false`; its child states at lines 84 and 85 are also unreachable, and no top-level initial path reaches the scope.
issues.reason: The supplied containment obligation is satisfied structurally, but the cross-view closed model shows the required collision avoidance scope and both required states are unreachable from any top-level initial entry. This is a semantic gap for the explicitly named collision avoidance scope, so it is represented as a derived reachability obligation rather than altering the containment contract.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance states must be contained within the collision avoidance system scope.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The scope has a valid local initial edge to collision_avoidance_deactive, but that local edge does not establish reachability from the model root.
issues.title: Collision avoidance states are unreachable from the model root

issues.basis: The NL6 termination contract names HighwayMode and FinishState as a termination relation. The closed inspection inventory binds FinishState to state:FinishState:line:21 and records outgoing transition:line:36 and transition:line:40. The source inventory also identifies FinishState as the HighwayMode completion target.
issues.expected: HighwayMode must terminate by reaching a stable FinishState with no continuation that re-enters or exits into continued behavior.
issues.observed: FinishState is reachable but has outgoing transitions to the enclosing final boundary on `urban_way=true` and `auto_finished=true`; the target is therefore not stable termination in the supplied closed model.
issues.reason: The required termination property is stronger than endpoint existence. The exact closed model reaches FinishState, but FinishState has outgoing transitions to the enclosing completion boundary under `urban_way=true` and `auto_finished=true`, so the designated completion state can continue rather than remain a stable termination point.
issues.requirement_quote: The HighwayMode ends when the system transitions to FinishState, triggered by the `auto_finished=true` condition.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The authored source explicitly describes HighwayMode as ending at FinishState, and the endpoint transition exists; if termination is interpreted as eventual entry only rather than stable completion, the outgoing FinishState behavior would not refute it.
issues.title: HighwayMode does not stably terminate at FinishState

issues.basis: NL12 defines the collision avoidance system scope and its two states. The source inventory and trace bind CollisionAvoidance plus both child states to exact closed refs. Inspection-equivalent and finite verification facts report CollisionAvoidance and both children unreachable from a top-level initial entry.
issues.expected: The collision avoidance states must be operationally available within the collision avoidance system scope.
issues.observed: CollisionAvoidance, collision_avoidance_deactive, and collision_avoidance_active are structurally present and nested, but all three are unreachable from the top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: The exact collision avoidance scope and both required states are present and contained, but the enclosing CollisionAvoidance composite is absent from top-level reachability. This is a behavioral scope consequence distinct from declaration or containment.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance states must be contained within the collision avoidance system scope.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The contract property itself is containment, and the supplied model does satisfy structural containment; the reachability fact may be a separate behavioral concern rather than a failure of containment.
issues.title: Collision avoidance scope is unreachable from the root

issues.basis: NL12 requires initial entry into collision_avoidance_deactive within the collision avoidance system. The closed model binds the local edge to transition:line:86 and its owner to CollisionAvoidance, while inspection-equivalent and verification facts show the owner and target are unreachable from top-level initialization.
issues.expected: The collision avoidance system must be entered from the top-level initialization context and then enter collision_avoidance_deactive.
issues.observed: The local initial edge exists, but CollisionAvoidance and collision_avoidance_deactive are unreachable from the top-level initial entry; no operational root path reaches this owner-local entry.
issues.reason: The authored collision avoidance scope has an exact local initial edge to collision_avoidance_deactive, but that scope itself is not reached from the top-level initial entry. A local child entry therefore does not establish operational root entry for the collision avoidance system.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system must initially enter collision_avoidance_deactive.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The exact owner-local initial edge is present and unconditional, so the narrow local initial-entry relation is satisfied if root reachability is outside the contract's intended scope.
issues.title: Collision avoidance has no reachable root entry

issues.basis: NL12 requires activation from collision_avoidance_deactive to collision_avoidance_active. The source and closed inventories bind the transition to transition:line:87. Event-consumer facts show the activation event has a declared consumer but an empty reachable consumer set, and finite verification refutes that consumer reachability.
issues.expected: When a stated danger condition occurs, a reachable consumer transition must activate collision_avoidance_active from collision_avoidance_deactive.
issues.observed: The declared activation consumer transition:line:87 exists, but its consumer state and transition are not reachable from a top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: The exact activation transition and both endpoint states exist, but the consumer state is unreachable from the top-level initial entry. Therefore the required danger response is not operationally available in the closed model.
issues.requirement_quote: A transition from collision_avoidance_deactive to collision_avoidance_active must exist when any stated danger condition is met.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The endpoint transition is present and carries the authored activation event projection; if the contract requires only structural transition existence, reachability is outside its narrow endpoint property.
issues.title: Collision activation consumer is unreachable

issues.basis: NL13 requires deactivation from collision_avoidance_active to collision_avoidance_deactive. The source and closed inventories bind the transition to transition:line:88. Event-consumer facts show a declared consumer with no reachable consumer transition, and finite verification refutes that reachability.
issues.expected: When all three inactive conditions hold, a reachable consumer transition must return to collision_avoidance_deactive.
issues.observed: The declared deactivation consumer transition:line:88 exists, but its consumer state and transition are not reachable from a top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: The exact deactivation transition and endpoint states exist, but the active-state consumer is unreachable from the top-level initial entry. The required recovery response is therefore not operationally available.
issues.requirement_quote: A transition from collision_avoidance_active to collision_avoidance_deactive must exist when front_inactive, rear_inactive, and pedestrian_inactive hold.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The exact endpoint relation and event projection are present; if the contract is read as a static transition-existence requirement, the separate consumer reachability defect is not an endpoint mismatch.
issues.title: Collision deactivation consumer is unreachable
